subject.title: fix(plugins): bound before_tool_call hook with a default timeout

question: Should `before_tool_call` get an unconditional 15s fail-closed default timeout for existing plugins?
rationale: The code path is the clean central fix for the wedge, but it intentionally changes existing plugin behavior from unbounded wait to denied tool call after 15s.

options.title: Accept 15s after proof
options.body: Land this default once the contributor adds a redacted live run, terminal transcript, or runtime log showing the after-fix timeout denial path.

options.title: Change the timeout policy
options.body: Require a longer budget, documented override, or compatibility path before changing existing plugin behavior.

options.title: Keep unbounded behavior for now
options.body: Pause or close the PR if maintainers decide slow existing plugins must not be denied by a new default timeout yet.

recommendation.title: Accept 15s after proof
recommendation.body: Land this default once the contributor adds a redacted live run, terminal transcript, or runtime log showing the after-fix timeout denial path.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the recent merger/co-author on the broad plugin hook files and is the strongest available owner for a compatibility tradeoff in this core plugin-runtime path.
